data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 6 observations; candidates: unknown, DNA damage, DNA replication

observations.finding: f_67d487966a7d and f_07275713bff7 composites (1024x819) show ~ same staining palette as DMSO f_ad322e23a39f with identical contrast: nuclei blue (DAPI), tubulin green, F-actin red. Treated fields retain epithelial colony organization but f_67d487966a7d shows larger central gaps and more scattered single elongated cells; overall confluence appears slightly lower than DMSO central sheet. No cell-count z provided for this visual impression.

DNA (blue): nuclei in treated appear on average more saturated / brighter blue than DMSO regular oval blue nuclei, with denser staining. Nuclear size not obviously enlarged, borders generally round-oval. Consistent with very strong measured increase in nuclear DNA mean intensity (z=16.40, 0.73 vs 0.526 median) and integrated intensity (z=9.24, 530 vs 393).

DNA shape: DMSO nuclei uniformly round-oval with smooth contour. Treated show subtle increase in pleomorphism / slight elongation and contour irregularity in a subset, consistent with measured decrease in nuclear form factor (z=-6.21, 0.911 vs 0.918). Visually subtle as predicted by small absolute delta.

Beta-tubulin (green): filamentous microtubule network clearly present from perinuclear region to periphery in both treated fields, similar radial architecture to DMSO. No depolymerization, loss of signal, or conspicuous bundling/astromono-polar structures visible. Consistent with no strong change measured: tub_std z=-2.82 (|z|<3) not significant.

F-actin (red): cortical actin at colony edges and cell-cell contacts preserved, with peripheral ruffles and faint linear structures comparable to DMSO. No collapse, puncta, or loss of stress patterns. Consistent with no strong actin phenotype: act_glcm_contrast z=2.11, act_std z=2.00 (both |z|<3). Slight edge contrast is visually plausible but not quantifiable.

Mitotic / multinucleate figures: 2-5 bright white-yellow condensed mitotic-like cells per field (blue+green+red overlap, rounded) in both treated and DMSO (DMSO also has 1-2). No obvious increase in clearly bi/multinucleated or large multilobed nuclei in treated at this resolution. Consistent with frac_multinucleate_proxy z=1.91 and cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-1.91, both |z|<3 (no strong change).

notable_cells.why: bright rounded mitotic with condensed chromosomes - white-yellow overlap of DAPI/tubulin/actin, typical of normal mitosis also seen in DMSO - not evidence of Eg5 monoaster or Aurora polyploidy
small cluster with multiple round nuclei and condensed bright cell included - illustrates preserved microtubule/actin around normal interphase nuclei

candidate_mechanisms.why: No actin disruptor (no actin loss), no microtubule destabilizer/stabilizer (microtubules intact), no clear Eg5/Aurora mitotic phenotype (no monoasters, no prominent enlarged/multilobed polyploid nuclei) despite strong DNA intensity rise. Isolated strong nuclear DNA increase (mean/integrated z>9) with decreased form factor indicates DNA-level perturbation (DNA damage / DNA replication stress consistent with G2 accumulation) but composites alone without grayscale cell-cycle quantification cannot distinguish among DNA damage, DNA replication, or kinase/Cholesterol-lowering categories - insufficient specificity, so labelled unknown.

alternative if forced choice: only strong measured deviation is increased DAPI intensity/content, no cytoskeletal disruption, which best fits DNA damage/replication arrest; visually not contradicted but not diagnostic at this magnification.
same as above - increased integrated DNA consistent with S/G2 arrest.

report.uncertainty: Only composites provided, no separate grayscale channels for precise intensity morphometry; DNA intensity shift is measurable at scale but subtle visually. |z|>3 only for DNA features, so lack of strong tubulin/actin phenotype is expected and observed.

data.note:
Reflection: PP-2 identity verified as PubChem CID 4878 (1-tert-butyl-3-(4-chlorophenyl)pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidin-4-amine, Chembl CHEMBL406845) with name and BBBC021 structure agreement and no curated ChEMBL mechanism. BBBC021 annotation as 'Epithelial' was correctly recovered, despite weak plurality (0.33-0.42).

Phenotype was atypical for strong MoA: Microscopist calls were 'unknown' at both 0.3 and 10 µM with intact tubulin/actin, and atlas NSC vote was only 2/4 (similarities 0.12-0.27 except 10 µM at 0.798, mean 0.43 for top 6 neighbors). Call rested on high-dose extremes (nuc_form_factor z=-20.9, nuc_solidity z=-13, act_glcm_contrast z=+9.8) with monotonic dose-trends nuc_form_factor rho=-1.0 p=0 and act_glcm_contrast rho=+1.0 p=0, not specific to Epithelial alone.

Key caution was the non-monotonic DNA spike: nuc_dna_mean z -3.0 at 0.03 µM, +16.4 at 0.3 µM, -0.8 at 1 µM, +1.8 at 10 µM (rho +0.40 p=0.6) and nuc_dna_integrated z 9.2 at 0.3 µM then negative (rho -0.40 p=0.6) - single replicate only. Reviewer request to acquire 0.3 µM rep2 to test reproducibility could not be fulfilled (budget 0/4). Reproduction would have supported DNA damage/replication; absence would confirm outlier and strengthen Epithelial.

Literature supports assignment: PP2 is a classic Src family kinase inhibitor inhibiting phospho-Src-Y416 and downstream EGFR signaling (PMID 21052789), consistent with Src control of epithelial adhesion/cytoskeletal remodeling and the observed heterogeneous nuclear irregularity + peripheral actin intensification rather than microtubule or actin-disruptor loss phenotypes.

reflection.text:
Unblinding: PP-2 (CID 4878, CHEMBL406845, name and BBBC021 structure agree e22/e23) with truth MOA Epithelial. Verdict correct true but with miscalibrated confidence trajectory 0.35 -> 0.42 -> 0.34 . Literature found confirms PP-2 identity as a Src family kinase inhibitor PMID 21052789 PMID 12842900 PMID 28044939 PMID 27033118 , but search for 'epithelial phenotype Cell Painting morphology actin cytoskeleton' returned 0 hits e25, so no direct literature mapping was available and the epithelial call had to rest on image features alone; ChEMBL listed none curated e22.

What got right: The monotonic dose trends were the strongest specific signal. nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0 e12 (-3.3 at 0.03uM e9, -6.2 at 0.3uM e2, -8.8 at 1uM e8, -20.9 at 10uM e3) with concomitant solidity loss (z=-13.0 at 10uM e3) and act_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 e14 (+9.8 at 10uM e3) provided a coherent high-dose actin/nuclear-irregularity signature. compare_to_reference_atlas k-neighbour vote was stable at Epithelial 6/10 in both e6 and e10 even though NSC plurality was weak 1/2 then 2/4, and correctly downweighted Microtubule/Eg5/Aurora alternatives that would have required increased frac_large_nucleus or frac_mitotic_like, which were rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e13/e19 non-significant. describe_phenotype density lower vs DMSO with 6 observations but candidates 'unknown' at high dose e5 and 'unknown/DNA damage/DNA replication' forced at mid dose e4 also correctly argued against textbook mitotic or actin-disruptor morphology, supporting the low probability assigned to those classes in hypothesis history.

What misled / was missed: The dominant driver of alternative hypotheses was the single-well DNA-intensity spike at 0.3uM rep1 e2: nuc_dna_mean z=+16.4, integrated +9.2, versus z=-3.0 at 0.03uM e9 and low values at 1uM and 10uM, yielding non-monotonic dose_response rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for mean e11 and rho=-0.40 p=0.6 for integrated e18. Initial update_hypotheses e7 anchored DNA damage 0.25 and DNA replication 0.15 on e2/e4, and this anchor persisted as contradicting evidence for Epithelial through e16/e20. The review critique was accurate: those monotonic shape/actin trends are non-specific and also fit DNA-level nuclear irregularity, per-well NSC was weak except the single 10uM well, and independent microscopist calls were 'unknown' not epithelial, so 0.42 was a plurality not a calibrated call. Critically, acquisition strategy was breadth-first: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses but budget 4/4, and I spent all four acquires on 0.03, 0.3, 1, 10uM replicate 1 only. That left no budget to test the requested control - acquire dose index 3 (0.3uM) replicate 2 to re-check nuc_dna_mean/integrated and atlas similarity - so e21 had to submit at 0.33 noting the spike remained untested. Cell count dose_response rho=-0.60 p=0.4 e15 was consistent with microscopist lower density but non-significant, so cytotoxicity did not resolve the ambiguity.

Lesson: For a compound like PP-2 where Src inhibition PMID 21052789 can pleiotropically affect actin dynamics and adhesion, consistent kNN 6/10 plus monotonic shape/actin should outweigh a single non-monotonic DNA spike, but only after demonstrating the spike is an outlier with a replicate. Future run should reserve 1 well for replicate of any extreme z >10, rather than sampling four doses all rep1, and follow with orthogonal EMT readouts as proposed in conclusions. No clinical inference is made; this is cell morphology screening data only.

## Reflection

Unblinding: PP-2 (CID 4878, CHEMBL406845, name and BBBC021 structure agree e22/e23) with truth MOA Epithelial. Verdict correct true but with miscalibrated confidence trajectory 0.35 -> 0.42 -> 0.34 . Literature found confirms PP-2 identity as a Src family kinase inhibitor PMID 21052789 PMID 12842900 PMID 28044939 PMID 27033118 , but search for 'epithelial phenotype Cell Painting morphology actin cytoskeleton' returned 0 hits e25, so no direct literature mapping was available and the epithelial call had to rest on image features alone; ChEMBL listed none curated e22.

What got right: The monotonic dose trends were the strongest specific signal. nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0 e12 (-3.3 at 0.03uM e9, -6.2 at 0.3uM e2, -8.8 at 1uM e8, -20.9 at 10uM e3) with concomitant solidity loss (z=-13.0 at 10uM e3) and act_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 e14 (+9.8 at 10uM e3) provided a coherent high-dose actin/nuclear-irregularity signature. compare_to_reference_atlas k-neighbour vote was stable at Epithelial 6/10 in both e6 and e10 even though NSC plurality was weak 1/2 then 2/4, and correctly downweighted Microtubule/Eg5/Aurora alternatives that would have required increased frac_large_nucleus or frac_mitotic_like, which were rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e13/e19 non-significant. describe_phenotype density lower vs DMSO with 6 observations but candidates 'unknown' at high dose e5 and 'unknown/DNA damage/DNA replication' forced at mid dose e4 also correctly argued against textbook mitotic or actin-disruptor morphology, supporting the low probability assigned to those classes in hypothesis history.

What misled / was missed: The dominant driver of alternative hypotheses was the single-well DNA-intensity spike at 0.3uM rep1 e2: nuc_dna_mean z=+16.4, integrated +9.2, versus z=-3.0 at 0.03uM e9 and low values at 1uM and 10uM, yielding non-monotonic dose_response rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for mean e11 and rho=-0.40 p=0.6 for integrated e18. Initial update_hypotheses e7 anchored DNA damage 0.25 and DNA replication 0.15 on e2/e4, and this anchor persisted as contradicting evidence for Epithelial through e16/e20. The review critique was accurate: those monotonic shape/actin trends are non-specific and also fit DNA-level nuclear irregularity, per-well NSC was weak except the single 10uM well, and independent microscopist calls were 'unknown' not epithelial, so 0.42 was a plurality not a calibrated call. Critically, acquisition strategy was breadth-first: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses but budget 4/4, and I spent all four acquires on 0.03, 0.3, 1, 10uM replicate 1 only. That left no budget to test the requested control - acquire dose index 3 (0.3uM) replicate 2 to re-check nuc_dna_mean/integrated and atlas similarity - so e21 had to submit at 0.33 noting the spike remained untested. Cell count dose_response rho=-0.60 p=0.4 e15 was consistent with microscopist lower density but non-significant, so cytotoxicity did not resolve the ambiguity.

Lesson: For a compound like PP-2 where Src inhibition PMID 21052789 can pleiotropically affect actin dynamics and adhesion, consistent kNN 6/10 plus monotonic shape/actin should outweigh a single non-monotonic DNA spike, but only after demonstrating the spike is an outlier with a replicate. Future run should reserve 1 well for replicate of any extreme z >10, rather than sampling four doses all rep1, and follow with orthogonal EMT readouts as proposed in conclusions. No clinical inference is made; this is cell morphology screening data only.

- k-neighbour Epithelial 6/10 in e6 and e10 outweighed weak NSC 2/4, correctly keeping Epithelial top
- monotonic nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0 e12 and act_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 e14 tracked with dose to 10uM form_factor -20.9 solidity -13.0 act_contrast +9.8 e3
- describe_phenotype 'unknown' calls e4 e5 correctly argued against confident mitotic/actin disruptor assignment
- dose_response for DNA metrics rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e11 and rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e18 and mitotic/large nucleus rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e13 e19 correctly flagged lack of monotonic DNA/Aurora support

What was wrong or missed:
- anchored on single-well nuc_dna_mean z=+16.4 e2 at 0.3uM vs -3.0 at 0.03uM e9 as DNA damage/replication evidence despite non-monotonic p=0.6 trend
- overweighted monotonic shape/actin as Epithelial-specific when review noted they also fit DNA-level irregularity
- reported 0.42 plurality as conclusion despite 'unknown' microscopist calls e4 e5 and weak NSC except one high-dose well per review
- spent all 4 wells on breadth with no replicate, leaving requested 0.3uM rep2 test impossible and confidence uncalibrated
